unit: no citywide boat-removal order
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale's code puts storm protection of a boat on its owner: a vessel at a municipal dock space must be protected by its owner once a hurricane warning is issued for Broward County. Boarding up openings for hurricane preparation during a watch or warning is carved out of the boarding-certificate rules, and a tidal flood barrier left in disrepair after a storm is a citable offence with fixed repair deadlines.

unit: minor-repair permit fee after a hurricane
qualifier: Miami Beach's fee schedule cuts the permit fee for minor repairs under $20,000 by 40% for three months after a hurricane event, though not for railing repairs, and repairs must be of substantially similar design. A seawall in disrepair is a citable offence: show progress in 60 days, file with the city and Miami-Dade DERM within six months, and finish substantial work within 730 days.
detail_rows: Post-hurricane fee cut :: Due to hurricane events, fees for minor repairs under a total value of $20,000.00 are reduced by 40% for three months from the hurricane event to pull the permit; it does not apply to permits for railing repairs, and all repairs must be of a substantially similar design, quality and appearance - Code Appendix A, Fee Schedule (fee in Sec. 14-62(c)) | Seawall duty :: All property owners must maintain seawalls, bulkheads, living shorelines and other shoreline protection in good repair; a wall is presumed in disrepair if it allows upland erosion, transfer of material through the wall, or tidal water to flow through or over it to the upland property or right-of-way - Sec. 54-63(a) | Repair clock :: After a notice of violation: demonstrate progress within 60 days (proposals, financing or permit applications count), submit permit applications to the Miami Beach Building Department and Miami-Dade RER (DERM) within six months, and where the substantial-improvement threshold is met, design, permit and build the improvements within 730 days of the citation - Sec. 54-63(a)

unit: to show progress / finish a cited seawall
qualifier: Delray Beach makes failing to maintain or repair a needed seawall a public nuisance, with 60 days to show progress and 365 days to finish after notice. Before each hurricane season owners must inspect their land and fix hazards; during a warning or alert, construction materials must be tied down, and in single-family districts dumpsters must be emptied and roof tiles strapped or removed. The city will not collect construction or demolition debris.
detail_rows: Seawall nuisance :: It is unlawful and a public nuisance to fail to erect, maintain or repair a seawall where a body of water requires one - necessary when the lack or condition of the wall endangers safety, navigability or swimming, allows upland erosion or transfer of material, or lets tidal water reach neighbours or the right-of-way. Show progress within sixty (60) days of notice and complete within three hundred sixty-five (365) days - Code Sec. 100.04 (Ord. 22-21) | Before the season :: Each year, prior to hurricane season, property owners shall inspect their properties and correct conditions that may be a hazard in hurricane winds; debris or vegetation that creates such a hazard is a nuisance - Sec. 100.02. Civil penalty: $250 uncontested, $325 contested - Sec. 37.39 | Warning or alert :: Construction materials and equipment shall be secured against displacement by wind - by guying and shoring and tying down loose materials, equipment and construction sheds - and loose outdoor objects lashed or stored - LDR Sec. 7.1.4(D)(1) | Single-family sites :: In the event of tropical storm or hurricane warnings the applicant/owner shall empty all dumpsters, remove or secure loose construction debris, materials and port-o-lets, and strap or remove all roof tiles - LDR Sec. 4.4.3(I)(5) | Not collected :: Building materials from construction, alteration or demolition will not be collected under the city's residential service; removal is the contractor's or installer's responsibility. Debris from minor do-it-yourself repairs is collected if bundled, with lumber no longer than four (4) feet and without nails - Sec. 51.20
source: City of Delray Beach Code of Ordinances Secs. 37.39, 51.20, 100.02, 100.04; Land Development Regulations Secs. 4.4.3, 7.1.4 (Municode)

unit: before predicted landfall to moor in city waterways
qualifier: Coral Gables makes boat owners responsible for securing their boats before a hurricane; boats using the city waterway for refuge must be securely moored no later than 24 hours before the officially predicted approach, and any damage from those moorings - including removal or salvage - is the boat owner's liability. Disaster debris on private property is the owner's responsibility, and tying a boat to someone else's dock or seawall without consent is unlawful.
detail_rows: Mooring for refuge :: Boats or watercraft using the city waterway for refuge will be securely moored not later than 24 hours prior to the officially predicted approach of a hurricane, with adequate equipment and safeguards; no such mooring constitutes official approval by the city - Code Sec. 86-87(b)(1)-(2) | Liability :: Damages to boats, property or persons flowing from hurricane moorings in the city waterway are the personal responsibility of the boat owner, including removal or salvage of the boat - Sec. 86-87(b)(3) | Someone else's dock :: It is unlawful to moor or tie a boat at a dock, piling or seawall of a property without the consent of the owner or person in control of the premises - Sec. 86-87(c) | Private-property debris :: Disaster-generated debris on private roads and private property is the responsibility of the property owner, who must rely heavily on private contractors; the city may remove it only on a declared immediate threat with right-of-entry and hold-harmless documentation, limited to living, recreational and working areas - Sec. 27-8 (Ord. 2017-42) | Shutters after the storm :: An occupied structure whose storm shutters have not been removed from the required means of escape after a hurricane watch or warning has expired is an unsafe structure - Sec. 105-89(7)
source: City of Coral Gables Code of Ordinances Secs. 27-8, 86-87, 105-89 (Municode)

unit: landscape debris must be gone
qualifier: Key Biscayne bans putting yard waste on or within ten feet of the right-of-way once a hurricane watch is issued, unless the Village Manager instructs otherwise in writing. Debris can sit on your own swale only for a licensed private hauler, and only if pickup is finished before a hurricane warning is issued, at the owner's cost.
detail_rows: Hurricane watch :: Once an official hurricane watch is issued by the National Weather Service for an area including the Village, no person shall place yard waste - clippings, trees, palm fronds, leaves, branches - on any portion of the public right-of-way or within ten feet of it, unless instructed in writing by the Village Manager - Code Sec. 8-301(a) | Private hauler exception :: Temporary placement on the swale beside the parcel that produced it is allowed for pickup by a licensed private hauler, so long as pickup and removal is fully accomplished before the National Weather Service issues an official hurricane warning and at the private property owner's sole cost - Sec. 8-301(a) | New homes :: Exotic vegetation listed in Exhibit A must be removed before a building permit is issued for a new single-family or duplex residence - Sec. 8-301(b)
source: Village of Key Biscayne Code of Ordinances Sec. 8-301, Article V Hurricane Protection Measures (Municode)

unit: before the city clears private-property debris
qualifier: Deerfield Beach clears disaster debris from public and private rights-of-way, and gated communities must give the city access during a declared emergency, but the city will not enter private property to remove debris until the owner signs a disaster debris removal agreement holding the federal government, state and city harmless. Tidal flood barriers must be kept in good repair, with 60 and 365 days to act after notice.

unit: loose lumber, trash and materials on a hurricane advisory
qualifier: Dania Beach requires every lot owner, occupied or not, to securely tie down loose lumber, trash and other materials once a hurricane advisory is issued for the Broward County area. Commercial construction sites must take down wind screening on a hurricane warning and put it back within ten days. A cited tidal flood barrier must show progress in 60 days and be repaired within 365.

unit: seasonal residents must secure loose objects

unit: beach-stored watercraft
qualifier: Juno Beach allows only non-motorized watercraft to be stored on the beach, by town permit, and owners must remove them on notice of a hurricane watch; failing to comply within 48 hours can cost the permit and lead to impoundment. After a declared disaster the town clears debris from public and private streets, with private-road owners holding the town harmless.
detail_rows: Beach storage :: Storage of nonmotorized watercraft on the beach requires a town permit; no motorized watercraft may be stored on the beach or dune - Code Sec. 18-100(a) | Hurricane watch :: Upon notification of a hurricane watch from the county's division of emergency management or area news weather stations, the owner shall remove the watercraft - Sec. 18-100(d)(4); failure to comply within 48 hours results in permit revocation and may result in boat impoundment - Sec. 18-100(d)(6) | Street debris :: After the mayor declares a state of emergency, the town may clear debris from public and private streets and rights-of-way, including private communities; owners of private roads hold the town harmless, and removal is limited to eliminating an imminent threat - Sec. 22-1 (Ord. 598)

unit: vessels may anchor during a hurricane watch
qualifier: Lake Worth Beach does not consent to any vessel anchoring or mooring in city waterways and requires those that do to be able to move under their own power and evacuate immediately in an emergency - but vessels seeking shelter or safe harbour during hurricanes or a hurricane watch or warning are exempt. Portable storage units must leave the city on a hurricane warning.
detail_rows: Anchoring rules :: Every vessel anchored or moored in city waterways must be able to navigate under its own power and immediately evacuate in an emergency, carry working lights and show a white all-round light visible two nautical miles at night - Code Sec. 22-3(a) | No consent :: The city does not consent to any vessel anchoring or mooring in city waterways and assumes no liability for them - Sec. 22-3(b) | Storm exception :: The prohibitions do not apply to vessels seeking shelter or safe harbor during hurricanes or periods of hurricane watch or warning issued by the National Weather Service, or to vessels in the Intracoastal Waterway - Sec. 22-3(b)(2), (4) (Ord. 2003-18) | Storage pods :: Portable storage units must be removed from the city immediately on a hurricane warning; removal is the owner/operator's responsibility - Sec. 23.4-18
source: City of Lake Worth Beach Code of Ordinances Secs. 22-3, 23.4-18 (Municode)

unit: strap rating for boats left on lifts
qualifier: Key Colony Beach makes owners responsible for securing boats and gear for storms, and if a hurricane watch is declared while an owner will be away more than a week, boats on lifts must be strapped with lines rated to 120 percent of the loaded boat's weight. A 2026 ordinance sets a seawall repair clock: safety measures in 15 days, engineer in 60, permit applications in 120, and completion within 12 months of permit approval.
detail_rows: Owners secure boats :: Owners are responsible for securing boats, boating equipment and appurtenances in storms or hurricanes; seasonal residents secure before leaving, and residents during the season secure before leaving for more than two (2) days - Code Sec. 5-8 (Ord. 295-1995) | Boats on lifts :: When a hurricane watch is declared and the owner is not available to secure the boat for more than one (1) week, boats on elevator lifts must be secured with line or straps rated to 120 per cent of the gross weight of boat and accessories, including fuel and water - Sec. 5-43(6) | Seawall clock :: On notice of an unsafe or deteriorated seawall: within 15 days install temporary safety measures; within 60 days retain a Florida professional engineer and submit an evaluation and plan; within 120 days submit all permit applications (including FDEP and/or Army Corps where applicable); complete within 12 months of permit approval. Extensions only for documented progress - Sec. 6-45(b)-(c) (Ord. 2026-509, 3-19-26) | Rentals :: Failure to comply can revoke a vacation rental licence or business tax receipt until full compliance - Sec. 6-45(e)
source: City of Key Colony Beach Code of Ordinances Secs. 5-8, 5-43, 6-45 (Municode)
